criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all governing approval rules, process facts, and authority statuses from the request and workspace records. The solver inspected registry.txt, record-17.txt, and record-22.txt, correctly applying the in-force record-17.txt (requiring Finance controller, Program Manager, and Purchase approvals for all price change requests) and rejecting the newer but unapproved draft record-22.txt (Purchase-only approval). In the operative sections, Gate 1 preserves TRSO sign-off by ER, Quality, and Purchase; Gate 5 preserves nomination sign-off by Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Manager; and Sections 4 and 5 explicitly enforce the three-party price change approval rule across all change tiers, including Tier 1 minor changes. Proposed tier thresholds and targets are properly framed as open points requiring CPO confirmation rather than invented facts.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Under the procedure in force (record-17, revision 2, approved 20 June 2025), every price change request needs approval from the Finance controller, the Program Manager and the Purchase team. All three are required. A later draft (record-22, revision 3) would let Purchase approve alone. It is unapproved, so this workflow does not use it. Tier 1 changes are therefore not exempt from this rule. They can be prepared automatically, but the three approvers must still sign. TechSol can make this a one-click approval, which saves time without changing the rules.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Purchase review. Finance and Program Manager are notified. Price change approval rules still apply (see below).

evidence.source_quote: TRSOs are reviewed and signed off by ER, Quality, and Purchase teams.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 1: TRSO sign-off by ER, Quality and Purchase. The module structure and a feature and variant roadmap are frozen as the baseline.

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 5: digital sign-off by Finance, Quality, ER and Program Manager.

criteria.consequence: None; governance rules and source constraints are preserved across both policy statements and operative workflow tables.
criteria.counterevidence: In the Section 4 table for Tier 1 Minor changes (word/document.xml:paragraph:72), the Approvals cell begins with 'Purchase review. Finance and Program Manager are notified.' However, the same cell immediately states 'Price change approval rules still apply (see below),' and Section 5 (word/document.xml:paragraph:82) explicitly confirms that Tier 1 changes are not exempt from record-17 and that all three approvers (Finance controller, Program Manager, and Purchase) must still sign.

criteria.rationale: The deliverable fulfills all substantive requirements of the prompt for both executive (CPO) and technical (TechSol) audiences. It diagnoses the lamp assembly post-nomination change bottleneck (up to 50% timeline extensions and manual paper tracking), defines a four-layer modular quotation structure (base assembly, feature modules, design element modules, and child parts/raw materials with associated cost drivers and index links), outlines a seven-step sourcing and nomination process with clear decision gates, establishes post-nomination flexibility points and change tiers, specifies parallel approval layers and price change governance, provides functional and integration requirements for the TechSol platform build, and clearly lists unresolved assumptions and open decisions for the CPO.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used. Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Suppliers quote a cost model, not one lump-sum price. The base lamp is quoted once. Each module is priced separately and can be added, removed or re-priced without re-quoting the whole assembly. The four module layers are listed below. Each module has a version number, a validity period and a named owner.

evidence.source_quote: As a first step, the CPO has asked you to develop the first-level workflow draft for this new sourcing process — both as a strategic process recommendation and as the foundational blueprint for the digital platform the TechSol will build.
evidence.output_quote: Core capabilities: a workflow engine with configurable gates, tiers and approval matrices, held in tables so that no code change is needed to alter them. A module and BOM-based cost model with version control. A supplier portal for quotes. Index feeds for raw materials. An immutable audit trail with digital signatures that meet Indian legal requirements. Role-based access. Dashboards that show where each file stands, how long it has been there, and which approvals are pending. Alerts and escalation. Integration with the ERP, PLM and BOM systems, and with the TRSO document store. Migration of existing paper files.

evidence.source_quote: Produce the requested professional deliverables, state unresolved assumptions, and do not invent missing facts.
evidence.output_quote: Confirm the tier thresholds and the time limits for approvals. Confirm whether the Purchase-only approval in the draft record-22 will be approved. If it is, the approval matrix is changed in configuration. Confirm the cycle time targets. Confirm the signature approach and the process for supplier onboarding to the portal.

criteria.consequence: None; the document is complete, coherent, and directly usable for CPO review and TechSol scoping.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are consistent and unambiguous; registry.txt clearly establishes record-17.txt as the operative approved rule and record-22.txt as an unapproved draft.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
